name: @candlelightgames/mcp

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Signs in to the user's Candlelight account (needed by every tool that reads or writes their content). Returns a link and code for the user to approve in their browser; show both to the user. Call again after they approve to check.

tools.name: sign_out
tools.description: Signs out: the stored sign-in is revoked and removed from this machine.

tools.name: reference
tools.description: The authoring guide, the vocabulary, shapes and worked examples. Without a name, lists what there is. Names: guide (read first; a player making a character reads player-guide instead), example/compact-campaign, vocabulary, vocabulary/<section>, term/<name>, values/<property> (place types and other fixed lists), shapes, shape/<name>, context, example/<name>, generators (the options of every generator kind), generator/<kind>. (ontology is the whole vocabulary as Turtle, about 170 KB: term/<name> and vocabulary/<section> say the same in a fraction of it.)

name.description: Which reference; omit to list them.

savePath.description: Write it (for the long examples) to this file instead of returning it.

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Checks a document on this machine, without sending it: that it parses (Turtle, JSON-LD or plain JSON), meets the vocabulary's shapes, and takes listed values (place types, a town's terrain) from their lists. Outlines what's in it. Free and fast: run it after every edit, before import_preview.

path.description: A file to read the content from (absolute, or relative to the working directory). Prefer this for anything longer than a few resources.

content.description: The content itself, when there is no file: Turtle, JSON-LD or plain JSON.

document.description: A document already uploaded to Candlelight (its `document` from upload_link or import_preview), instead of sending it again.

contentType.description: What the content is. From the file's extension when not given (.ttl, .jsonld, .json); Turtle for inline content that isn't JSON.

tools.name: import_preview
tools.description: A dry run of the import on Candlelight's server: what it would create, update and remove, and what the importer would drop (droppedPredicates: things the app has nowhere to keep yet). It also runs validate's checks (checks), so there's no need to validate first. Nothing is saved to the account. Inline content is kept for a day as a `document`: pass that to import instead of sending the content again. Tell the user what would be dropped, and for an update, everything under removed: if it lists anything they didn't ask to remove, don't import.

path.description: A file to read the content from (absolute, or relative to the working directory). Prefer this for anything longer than a few resources.

content.description: The content itself, when there is no file: Turtle, JSON-LD or plain JSON.

document.description: A document already uploaded to Candlelight (its `document` from upload_link or import_preview), instead of sending it again.

contentType.description: What the content is. From the file's extension when not given (.ttl, .jsonld, .json); Turtle for inline content that isn't JSON.

campaignId.description: Into this campaign (you must be its GM). Without it, a document with an st:Campaign becomes a new campaign; anything else goes to the user's library.

sessionId.description: With campaignId: scenes no session in the content claims go into this session.

chapterId.description: With campaignId: places and scenes no chapter in the content claims go here.

mode.description: merge (the default) adds everything and leaves what is there alone, except a map the document carries for a town the campaign already has, which replaces that town's map (and moves its places onto the new buildings). update brings rows imported from the same subjects up to date (play state is never touched) and overwrites the GM's edits to the fields it supplies. For a campaign import made (it has a module of its own) it removes only what came from that module and the document no longer has; for one made otherwise it can remove anything imported without a module. Send the whole original document, never a fragment, and preview it first.

tools.name: import
tools.description: Imports a document into the user's Candlelight account, all or nothing: a new campaign (a document with an st:Campaign), into an existing campaign (campaignId), or into their library. Afterwards, as the app does: towns it creates have their maps drawn and their people housed, and the campaign's scenes set at one place in a town get battlemaps. Other scenes are listed with what their maps could be made from (make_scene_map). Preview first, and confirm with the user before importing into an existing campaign. With mode update, import only what the preview's removed list says the user wants removed.

drawTownMaps.description: Draw the maps of the towns it creates (default true), as the app does.

makeSceneMaps.description: Make battlemaps for the campaign's scenes set at one town place, once its towns are drawn (default true).

tools.name: generate
tools.description: Runs one of Candlelight's procedural generators, saving nothing. Kinds with a vocabulary form (town, establishment, monster, location-npcs, related-npc, npc-house, town-building, town-housing, town-map) come back as JSON-LD, ready to edit and import, and character as an st:CharacterSheet in Turtle (as read_character_sheet gives one); the rest as the generator's plain output, to write into the vocabulary. Seeded: the same seed and options give the same result. Each kind takes its own options: read the reference generator/<kind> (or generators, for all of them) before passing any. Kinds: monster, location, town, room, item, spell, feat, background, companion, hazard, chapter, encounter-table, loot-table, battle-map, weapon, npc, npc-profile, establishment, location-npcs, tavern, hook, clue, dungeon, character, appearance, dungeon-npc, trap, encounter, loot, campaign-chapter, module-doc, location-scene, shop, town-stats, town-quests, district-name, town-housing, town-map, town-building, npc-house, related-npc.

options.description: The generator's options, which depend on the kind: `reference generator/<kind>` lists a kind's, `reference generators` every kind's. An option the kind doesn't take is refused. For example town: { townSize: 'city', townTerrain: 'coastal', townStyle: 'medieval' }.

seed.description: A seed, to get the same result again.

campaignId.description: For this campaign: its system, and its party's level for loot and shops.

systemSlug.description: The game system, when not the campaign’s.

savePath.description: Write the JSON-LD to this file instead of returning it.

tools.name: get
tools.description: GETs a path of Candlelight's API as the user. Useful paths: /api/campaigns (theirs), /api/campaigns/{id} (with format turtle: the whole campaign as a document, to extend and import back), /api/chapters?campaignId=, /api/sessions?campaignId=, /api/scenes?campaignId=, /api/towns?campaignId=, /api/towns/{id}, /api/users/me. JSON comes without the app's own copies of fields (a stored `cluesJson` beside its parsed `clues`, a scene's `rdfGraphNquads`); a list of scenes is long, so name the fields you need.

path.description: The API path, starting /api/ (a query string is fine).

format.description: json (the default), or turtle / json-ld for an export.

fields.description: JSON only: just these fields of each resource (e.g. ["id", "name", "mapId"]). Any field can be named, the left-out ones too.

full.description: JSON only: the response exactly as the API sent it, every field.

savePath.description: Write the response to this file instead of returning it.

tools.name: make_scene_maps
tools.description: Makes battlemaps for every scene set at one place in one of the campaign's towns that has no map yet, as import does, and lists the other scenes (set at several places, or not in a town) with what their maps could be made from. Maps are optional: tables that play in person or on another VTT may not want them.

tools.name: make_scene_map
tools.description: Without choice: lists what the scene's map could be made from (each of its places' buildings, the road out of a town, a kind of wilderness), the likeliest first. With choice: makes that map and puts it on the scene, with the scene's encounter and loot as tokens. A scene that has a map keeps it unless replace is true; the old map is kept in the campaign's maps either way.

choice.description: Which of the listed choices to make.

replace.description: Make a new map for a scene that has one (the old one stays in the campaign's maps, for the GM to delete or reuse).

separate.description: Make this scene its own map even when another scene already has a map of the same building (by default it shares that one).

tools.name: place_scene_tokens
tools.description: Brings the scene map's encounter and loot tokens in step with the scene, as saving the scene does in the app: a token for each creature in its encounters and each loot drop. A creature whose encounter row starts in a room of the map (set_encounter_rooms) goes at that room's centre, spread over its free cells; the rest go in free cells from the map's corner, for the GM to move. Maps made by make_scene_map(s), and maps a document brings to import, already have them; use this after changing a scene's encounter or its rooms (set_encounter_rooms, set_map_rooms), or for a map made before.

tools.name: view_map
tools.description: A scene's or a map's battlemap: its grid (columns × rows of cells, x from the left and y from the top, both from 0), its rooms (zones, each with an id and a rectangle of cells), the tokens on it, and its picture when it has one, with how the picture sits on the grid (`picture.howToCount`). Look at it to decide where rooms are (set_map_rooms) and where an encounter starts (set_encounter_rooms).

mapId.description: A map's id, instead of a scene's.

tools.name: set_map_rooms
tools.description: Names the rooms of a map as rectangles of cells (x1,y1 to x2,y2, inclusive, as view_map counts them), for an encounter to start in (set_encounter_rooms) and for the GM's room notes and fog. A room with an id view_map listed is redrawn and renamed; one without is added. Look at the map first (view_map); generated maps often have their rooms already.

tools.name: set_encounter_rooms
tools.description: Sets the room (of the scene's map, by the id view_map or set_map_rooms gave) each of the scene's encounter rows starts in, and optionally the round it arrives (3 for a dragon through the ceiling in round 3). A row is named by its creature ("Ninth Blade raiders") or its id. Then place_scene_tokens puts them in their rooms; in Candlelight the GM's scene review offers Place encounter. In a file, the same is st:startsInZone and st:arrivesRound on a stat-block mapping.

row.description: The row's creature name, or its id.

roomId.description: The room it starts in; null to clear it.

arrivesRound.description: The round it joins; 1 or null for the start.

tools.name: draw_town_map
tools.description: Draws a town's map on this machine and saves it, then houses its people: a town with no map in full (a city district by district), one partway drawn its remaining districts, a complete one nothing. `import` already does this for the towns it creates. redraw draws it all again, replacing the stored map: ask the GM first.

redraw.description: Draw it all again over the stored map (its places are moved to the new buildings).

tools.name: upload_link
tools.description: A link to upload a file to Candlelight yourself, outside this conversation (with curl, from a workspace that can reach the link's host, Candlelight's API), so its bytes never pass through you: the GM's artwork (as upload_image, without the base64), or a document to check and import, named afterwards by its `document` instead of sent whole. Give the file's exact size in bytes: the link is signed for that size and type, and works for 5 minutes. Run its `check` command first: anything but 200 (a 403 from the workspace's network proxy, say) means the workspace can't reach Candlelight, and `fallback` says what to do instead. Then PUT the file to uploadUrl with the Content-Type it gives.

filename.description: Its name, with an extension that says its type: map.webp, campaign.ttl.

bytes.description: The file's exact size in bytes (wc -c).

purpose.description: What it is for: document for something to import (Turtle, JSON-LD or JSON), character_sheet for a character sheet PDF to read (read_character_sheet), else as upload_image (default background_image).

tools.name: check_character
tools.description: Checks each st:CharacterSheet in a document against its system's rules, through Candlelight: its level, ability scores and hit points, and its spells against its class's list, the levels its slots reach and how many it knows or prepares (D&D 5e; the counts are 2014's). Sends only what the rules read, not the document. Each problem is an error (the sheet can't be that: fix it with the player) or a warning (ask the player, who settles it with their GM). Run it with validate before importing a character.

path.description: A file to read the content from (absolute, or relative to the working directory). Prefer this for anything longer than a few resources.

content.description: The content itself, when there is no file: Turtle, JSON-LD or plain JSON.

document.description: A document already uploaded to Candlelight (its `document` from upload_link or import_preview), instead of sending it again.

contentType.description: What the content is. From the file's extension when not given (.ttl, .jsonld, .json); Turtle for inline content that isn't JSON.

tools.name: ability_scores
tools.description: Works out a D&D 5e character's ability scores so you never add them up yourself: the scores it starts with (the standard array, point buy or rolls, as the player placed them), then each increase in level order (a 2024 background's bonuses, each level's Ability Score Improvement, a half feat's +1), giving the scores and modifiers after each. With `next` (the increase the player is choosing now: its level, and whether it's an ASI or a feat's +1), it also lists the ways to split it from the scores at that point, best first: a modifier rises only at an even score, so the split that raises the most modifiers comes first, and a tie goes to the class's main ability. Show the player the tally, and ask one increase at a time in level order.

base.description: The six scores before any increase: { str, dex, con, int, wis, cha }.

increases.description: The increases the player has placed. Applied in level order.

source.description: What it is: "Charlatan background", "Ability Score Improvement", "Fey Touched".

level.description: The character level it comes at (a background: 1).

bonus.description: What the player chose: { cha: 1, con: 1 }.

next.description: The increase the player is choosing now; placed after every increase at its level or before.

points.description: 2 for an ASI, 1 for a half feat, 3 for a 2024 background.

maxPerAbility.description: 2 for an ASI or background, 1 for a half feat.

among.description: The abilities it may go to (a background's three, a feat's choices); all six when absent.

prefer.description: The class's main abilities, first first (a warlock: ['cha', 'con']).

tools.name: join_campaign
tools.description: Joins the user to a campaign with the invite they were given (its link, or the token in it), as a player. Call it first without join: it says which campaign it is, who runs it, and whether they're in it already; tell the player, and call again with join: true only once they say so. A draft campaign takes no players yet: keep their character on their shelf (import with no campaign) to add later.

invite.description: The invite link (…/invite/…, …/join/…) or its token.

join.description: True to join, once the player has said yes. Without it, only reads the invite.

tools.name: add_character
tools.description: Puts one of the user's characters (a sheet on their shelf: the characterSheets an import made) into a campaign they're in, as its player; the campaign's GMs are told. Confirm the character and the campaign with the player first. A campaign they're not in is refused: join it first (join_campaign), or leave the character on their shelf. With a Session Zero running, its concept pitch and intro hook go with it.

characterId.description: The character sheet's id (the import's characterSheets).

campaignId.description: The campaign (join_campaign gives it, or get /api/campaigns).

conceptPitch.description: Session Zero: the character in a sentence or two, for the table.

introHook.description: Session Zero: how they come into the story.

tools.name: read_character_sheet
tools.description: Reads a character sheet PDF into an st:CharacterSheet, as Turtle, saving nothing: its scores, hit points, skills and saves, features, limited uses, equipment and spells, matched to the SRD by Candlelight. It reads D&D Beyond's PDF, the official 2014 and 2024 sheets, and Demiplane's Pathfinder 2e, Starfinder 2e and Daggerheart sheets; an SW5e or Cyberpunk RED sheet is imported in Candlelight itself. Put the Turtle in the campaign document (linked by the campaign's st:hasPlayerCharacter), never a bare st:PlayerCharacter, then check and import as usual. Give the PDF by its path: it is read on this machine and never sent anywhere; only what was read goes to Candlelight, to be matched.

path.description: The PDF's path (relative to where this server runs).

document.description: An uploaded PDF (upload_link with purpose character_sheet).

subject.description: The IRI to write the sheet under: the one the campaign document already gives this character, so importing it updates that character. A new one when left out.

system.description: The campaign's system (dnd5e2024, pathfinder2e, daggerheart…), when the sheet's format alone can't tell.

tools.name: upload_image
tools.description: Uploads the user's own artwork to Candlelight and returns its URL, for a document to import: a battlemap's picture (a map's st:backgroundImageUrl, instead of a generated one), a token's picture (st:tokenImageUrl), a handout's image or PDF (st:handoutMediaUrl), a character's portrait (st:avatarUrl), or a campaign's banner (st:coverImageUrl). Give the file by its path. PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG (a handout also takes PDF); up to 5 MB for a background, 8 MB for a battle map, 1 MB for a token, 15 MB for a handout. Uploads count against the GM's storage (2 GB free, 50 GB for Supporters): a refusal for space says how much is left, so tell the GM rather than retrying. Upload only images the GM gave you or asked for.

content.description: The image itself, as base64 (a data: URL is fine).

filename.description: Its name, if not the file’s own (the extension says its type).

purpose.description: What it is for (default background_image): background_image or battle_map for a map, token_image, handouts, avatar for a character's portrait, campaign_cover for a campaign's banner.

tools.name: town_map_svg
tools.description: Renders a town's stored map as SVG, with labels, for a campaign document or a printed adventure, to a file. The map must have been drawn (draw_town_map).

labels.description: Name the streets and places (default true).

instructions: Candlelight is a tabletop RPG platform. These tools help write campaigns and library content (NPCs, monsters, items, towns) for the user and import them into their Candlelight account. Start with `reference guide`, talk the story through with the user before writing, then validate, preview and import. Nothing is saved until `import`.
